subject: Transportation Systems
title: The Commuter Rail Boom
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Commuter Rail Boom.

hook.text: As cities sprawled, millions of workers needed to reach downtown every morning. Trains delivered.

buildup.text: Mumbai's locals, Tokyo's Yamanote, and London's Overground each move millions of riders daily.

discovery.text: A single rail line can carry 50,000 people per hour. No highway lane comes close.

twist.text: Capacity has limits. Tokyo employs professional pushers to squeeze riders into packed cars.

climax.text: Cities worldwide are expanding commuter rail to fight traffic congestion and cut emissions.

punchline.text: The daily commute is rail's most reliable market.

quiz.question: Why is commuter rail expanding globally?
options: It fights congestion and cuts emissions
